T1.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare the serial baseline with an OpenMP outer loop using the passed threads value as a hard CPU budget; start with static scheduling and retain a serial path for one thread or small n. Avoid thresholds tied to published test values. Measure available valid n/thread cases under the frozen protocol, verify complete output writes and varied-input correctness, and report overhead as well as any gain. Preserve correct variants for later combination even if they lose in isolation.
T1.subject: OpenMP scaling and overhead within the threads budget

T2.objective: Keep threading unchanged and compare the ordinary per-option loop as compiled by the frozen build with an explicit x86-intrinsics kernel. Use only ISA supported by the frozen target/build, with compile-time guards and a scalar fallback; do not change compiler flags or add runtime environment/ISA probing. Preserve the supplied Black-Scholes computation and CND coefficients. If vector math requires altered rounding, validate it against tolerance on varied inputs and retain a correct fallback. Measure each route separately so G can test combinations with T1 and T3.
T2.subject: Compiler-vectorized versus explicit SIMD execution

T3.objective: Keep this tree scalar-focused. Test sharing sqrtf(T) and Horner evaluation of the supplied CND polynomial as separate changes and in combination; preserve the formula and coefficients, and validate rounding on varied inputs. Judge changes by measured correctness and time rather than assuming the compiler does or does not already combine operations. Retain correctness-passing rewrites that are slightly slower alone if they could enable a later measured combination with T1 or T2.
T3.subject: Isolated scalar arithmetic rewrites and combination candidates

Gm1.objective: Partir du candidat T1, le plus rapide parmi ces sources mesurées, et y intégrer le noyau SIMD T2 sans perdre le budget de threads ni la couverture complète des sorties. Évaluer ce programme combiné avec le protocole inchangé; ne pas présumer que les gains s’additionnent.
Gm1.stop_condition: Arrêter cette combinaison si elle échoue à la correction ou n’améliore pas de manière fiable T1 seul; conserver alors le meilleur candidat correctement mesuré.
Gm1.subject: Combiner le parallélisme T1 et le noyau SIMD T2

Gm2.objective: Partir de Gm1, déjà mesuré à 1,060 ms, et tester si la variante T2 3b9fd1eef6f24d23 apporte une amélioration supplémentaire. Préserver le budget de threads, la couverture des sorties et la correction; mesurer selon le protocole inchangé.

Gm2.subject: Tester la variante T2 la plus rapide sur la base Gm1

mission.hypothesis: Prior OpenMP variants with per-worker grain thresholds have similar aggregate means, but available timings do not establish the serial/parallel crossover by size. This experiment tests a contrasting fixed total-work cutoff: keep the serial path below 2048 options, then request the full passed thread budget (capped by n) with static scheduling. It may avoid region overhead for smaller inputs while improving use of the budget on larger inputs; no gain is assumed.

retained: Replaced per-worker grain-based team sizing with a generic fixed total-work serial cutoff of 2048 options.
Above the cutoff, use static OpenMP scheduling with a team capped at min(threads, n); retain the serial path for one-or-fewer threads and small inputs.
Preserved the per-option computation and one distinct output write per loop iteration.

model_interpretation.hypothesis: Prior OpenMP variants with per-worker grain thresholds have similar aggregate means, but available timings do not establish the serial/parallel crossover by size. This experiment tests a contrasting fixed total-work cutoff: keep the serial path below 2048 options, then request the full passed thread budget (capped by n) with static scheduling. It may avoid region overhead for smaller inputs while improving use of the budget on larger inputs; no gain is assumed.

retained: Replaced per-worker grain-based team sizing with a generic fixed total-work serial cutoff of 2048 options.
Above the cutoff, use static OpenMP scheduling with a team capped at min(threads, n); retain the serial path for one-or-fewer threads and small inputs.
Preserved the per-option computation and one distinct output write per loop iteration.

mission.hypothesis: The selected explicit SSE2 parent computes four powers and a sum-of-products for each CND polynomial evaluation. Rewriting that same supplied polynomial in Horner form may reduce SIMD multiply instructions while leaving scalar logf/expf, the Black-Scholes formula, threading and the ordinary serial fallback unchanged. The altered rounding must pass varied-input tolerance checks; it may not improve performance, especially if scalar math remains dominant.

retained: Changed only the SSE2 CND polynomial evaluation to Horner form using the original coefficients.
Kept the ordinary scalar loop, scalar transcendental calls, explicit SIMD option kernel, SSE2 compile-time guard, fallback and tail handling unchanged.

model_interpretation.hypothesis: The selected parent (5742ad4218cf4186) runs serial whenever the full requested team would average fewer than 256 options per worker. Instead, cap the static OpenMP team to the number of 256-option work grains available, using the serial path only when that yields fewer than two workers. This tests whether partial use of the passed thread budget can parallelize medium workloads without idle workers, while preserving the existing generic grain and complete output coverage. Prior aggregate OpenMP means are close; no gain is assumed.

retained: Kept the serial path for nonpositive n, one-thread budgets, and work insufficient for at least two 256-option grains.
Set the OpenMP team size to min(threads, n / 256), allowing partial use of the passed budget instead of switching directly from the full team to serial.
Retained static scheduling, a team no larger than the passed thread budget, and one distinct output write per loop iteration.

mission.hypothesis: L’intégration des approximations SSE2 de log/exp de T2 dans le chemin par blocs à équipe OpenMP plafonnée de Gm1 peut réduire le coût des transcendantes scalaires pour les blocs sûrs. Le résultat autonome de T2 étant plus lent que Gm1, cette combinaison doit être mesurée sans présumer d’un gain. La réparation const-correcte permet aux replis scalaires de compiler.

retained: Retient l’équipe OpenMP plafonnée, l’ordonnancement statique, le seuil de travail et la couverture SIMD/queue scalaire de Gm1.
Intègre les approximations SSE2 de log et exp de T2 avec contrôles de domaine et replis scalaires pour les blocs non sûrs et les sorties restantes.
Rend const les pointeurs d’entrée du noyau scalaire afin que les replis depuis le noyau SSE2 compilent sans modifier les entrées.

retained: Reduced the generic minimum work grain from 512 to 64 options per worker so the bounded static OpenMP team can scale earlier.

model_interpretation.hypothesis: Capping the static OpenMP team by a generic 512-options-per-worker grain may reduce parallel overhead for intermediate workloads while still using the full passed thread budget for sufficiently large work. Unlike a serial-only cutoff, this tests a smaller team at the crossover region; no gain is assumed, and the controller should measure overhead, varied-input correctness, and output coverage.

retained: Factored the unchanged per-option Black-Scholes calculation into a shared inline helper for serial and parallel execution.
Added a static-scheduled OpenMP outer loop with a team size capped by both the passed thread budget and n/512.
Retained a serial path for nonpositive sizes, budgets of one or less, and workloads too small to support two workers at the selected grain.

mission.hypothesis: Combining T1’s capped OpenMP team and 256-options-per-worker cutoff with four-option SSE2 arithmetic may reduce arithmetic overhead on large inputs, but scalar logf/expf calls and interaction with threading may limit or erase the benefit. The combined program needs its own measurement.

retained: Retained T1’s inline per-option helper, serial cutoff and static OpenMP path with team size capped by min(threads, n).
Added a compile-guarded four-option SSE2 Black-Scholes kernel using unaligned loads, vector arithmetic and CND polynomial evaluation, while retaining scalar logf and expf calls.
Scheduled complete four-option blocks across the capped OpenMP team, handled the final one to three outputs scalarly, and retained scalar parallel fallback for unsupported targets.

model_interpretation.hypothesis: Combining T1’s capped OpenMP team and 256-options-per-worker cutoff with four-option SSE2 arithmetic may reduce arithmetic overhead on large inputs, but scalar logf/expf calls and interaction with threading may limit or erase the benefit. The combined program needs its own measurement.

retained: Retained T1’s inline per-option helper, serial cutoff and static OpenMP path with team size capped by min(threads, n).
Added a compile-guarded four-option SSE2 Black-Scholes kernel using unaligned loads, vector arithmetic and CND polynomial evaluation, while retaining scalar logf and expf calls.
Scheduled complete four-option blocks across the capped OpenMP team, handled the final one to three outputs scalarly, and retained scalar parallel fallback for unsupported targets.

mission.hypothesis: The full SSE2 math route measured 2.662 ms and the SIMD arithmetic route retaining scalar transcendental calls measured 5.631 ms, versus the 7.529 ms scalar baseline. This candidate tests a narrower bottleneck: keep scalar logf, sqrtf, and discount expf calculations, but evaluate both CND exponentials and polynomials with guarded SSE2. It may offer a different accuracy/performance tradeoff; speed and tolerance compliance are unmeasured.

retained: Kept the scalar Black-Scholes routine intact as the unsupported-build, unsafe-range, and tail fallback.
Added an SSE2 four-option path that computes d1, d2, and discount values with scalar math while vectorizing the supplied CND polynomial and its exponential approximation.
Guarded the vector CND exponential to [-80, 0], falling back to the scalar routine for any four-option group outside that range.
Kept threading, the entrypoint contract, and compiler flags unchanged.

model_interpretation.hypothesis: The independent option calculations can be distributed with a static OpenMP outer loop, while num_threads(threads) caps the requested team at the passed budget. A serial path for one thread and fewer than 512 options per requested thread should avoid paying parallel-region overhead on small workloads. Each loop iteration writes exactly its own result index; the controller still needs to verify correctness and measure the tradeoff.

retained: Extracted the per-option Black-Scholes expression into an inline helper used by both execution paths.
Added an OpenMP outer loop with schedule(static) and num_threads(threads), assigning each iteration a unique output element.
Retained a serial path for nonpositive work, one or fewer threads, and fewer than 512 options per requested thread.

hypotheses.claim: Un chemin série pourrait rester utile aux petites tailles pour éviter le coût OpenMP, mais aucun crossover n’est établi par les mesures visibles.
hypotheses.proposed_test: Comparer série et OpenMP sur des tailles intermédiaires disponibles, avec budgets de 1, 2 et 4 threads, mesures appariées et contrôle des sorties sur des entrées variées. Ne pas choisir le seuil à partir des tailles publiées.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Ne retenir aucun seuil si le gain n’est pas répétable au-delà de la variation mesurée; écarter la variante en cas d’échec de correction, de garde ou de respect du budget threads.

observations.claim: Les cinq essais T1 du catalogue sont déclarés valides et corrects. Le meilleur temps moyen rapporté est celui de 2a2949b870444487 (0,001400686 s; score 0,84314); les autres essais vont de 0,001403812 à 0,001450097 s. Le baseline rapporte 0,007528638 s. Ce sont des résultats de recherche, pas une confirmation finale.

Pour l’essai 2a, les journaux visibles rapportent 8 contrôles corrects, sans erreur, avec gardes intactes et entrées inchangées, sur n=16, 128, 1024 et 131072. À n=131072, les échantillons à 1 thread vont de 0,002952 à 0,003013 s et ceux à 4 threads de 0,000752 à 0,000754 s. Aucun temps de petite taille n’est visible.

uncertainties: La page de preuve de 2a est paginée et seule la première tranche est visible; le détail des autres essais n’est pas disponible ici.
Aucun crossover série/OpenMP sur petite taille, audit explicite des écritures complètes ou résultat de confirmation indépendante n’est visible.

contract.statement:
Optimize the supplied baseline on AMD EPYC 9654 with GCC 14.2. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Compute the exact supplied FP32 Black-Scholes implementation with its CND approximation. input1 contains 5 consecutive arrays of length n: S,X,T,r,v; output is n floats. Match abs error <=.001+5e-5*abs(reference). Performance uses published constants [100,98,2,.02,5]; correctness also tests varied per-element inputs. All entries must be processed, with no hardcoded output.
Edit only src/candidate.cpp. Keep extern C void run(const void*input1,const void*input2,void*output,int n,int parameter,int threads). Respect the threads argument as the CPU thread budget. Inputs are read-only and 64-byte aligned. Overwrite the full specified output on every call; no cached answers, external tools or libraries, filesystem, environment inspection, timing inspection or phase detection. Ordinary C++17, OpenMP and x86 intrinsics are available. Do not modify the protected correctness or timing protocol. Scratch allocation inside run is allowed and included in timing. The harness measures native wall-clock time, excluding input generation, oracle and compilation. Search and confirmation use different seeds. Numerical tolerances are fixed. The optimized reference source is withheld. Choose topics independently, record failed attempts, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G.
